decisions.scope: Forward-only governance correction only for the already accepted P2-004 Authentication Session Foundation contract after the contract's mandatory current-provider reconciliation identified a required Next.js Proxy path and current Supabase SSR identity/session requirements. decisions.decision: Preserve DEC-20261003-P2-004-AUTHENTICATION-SESSION-FOUNDATION-CONTRACT unchanged as historical accepted evidence. Correct the rolling WI-P2-004-AUTHENTICATION-SESSION-FOUNDATION contract by adding completed prerequisite WI-P0-NEXTJS-SEPTEMBER-2026-SECURITY-PATCH and changing the later implementation envelope from five paths to exactly six paths by adding apps/web/proxy.ts. The later runtime dependency targets are @supabase/supabase-js ^2.117.2 and @supabase/ssr ^0.12.7. The later Supabase server boundary must use createServerClient with current getAll/setAll cookie handling. Proxy is limited to authentication-session refresh through supabase.auth.getClaims(), request-cookie propagation, response-cookie propagation, and required cache-header propagation; it must not perform redirects, route authorization, capability authorization, or Rosuno business authorization. Trusted Rosuno authentication identity is only verified claims.sub exposed as an opaque subject and fails closed on provider error, absent/unusable claims, or absent/unusable sub. getSession() must not establish trusted identity. P2-003 remains the owner of authorization. Preserve the existing opaque-subject, fail-closed, no-token-leak, no-cross-request-global-cache, synthetic zero-live-network-test, business-state-neutrality, Gate 5 N/A, and Gate 6 N/A boundaries.
decisions.rationale: The original P2-004 decision intentionally required STOP and fresh Gate 0 reconciliation if current provider guidance required an additional dependency, path, or architectural change. After the separate Next.js 16.3.8 security prerequisite completed, fresh official Supabase SSR guidance confirmed that Next.js Server Components cannot write refreshed Auth cookies and requires a Next.js Proxy for session refresh. Current guidance uses getClaims() for trusted identity/session refresh, requires request and response cookie propagation, requires refreshed cache headers to survive response replacement, and warns against trusting getSession() as server-side identity verification. The smallest authority-consistent correction is therefore a forward-only six-path contract without adding a second provider helper path or moving authorization into Proxy.
decisions.impact: If later protected and accepted, this correction governs only the future bounded P2-004 application implementation contract. It does not itself install @supabase packages, modify apps/web/package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml, create apps/web/proxy.ts or any application source/test file, implement authentication UI or account workflows, alter P2-003 authorization ownership, create credentials/secrets, contact or mutate Supabase Auth or any database/environment, touch Staging/Production/OLD, alter P1-012, resolve G-1 through G-5 or F-01/F-02/F-03, or implement Founding Attorney, beta, survey, Arizona-page, onboarding, verification, pricing, availability, Live Now, marketplace, visibility, launch, or other draft Arizona launch-strategy functionality.
